Combine SIR Results of Multiple Antimicrobials

Source: R/sir_combine.R
sir_combine.Rd

Combine the SIR results of two or more antimicrobials into one SIR result per isolate, e.g. to create a variable for the combination therapy of piperacillin/tazobactam with gentamicin. The result is the best result of the antimicrobials, as a combination therapy covers the isolate if any of its antimicrobials is active. See Combination Therapy below for the exact rules.

The same rules are used by antibiogram() and wisca() for combination antibiograms, and by the count_*() and proportion_*() functions when more than one variable is used, so the result of sir_combine() can be used in any further analysis.

Usage

sir_combine(
  ...,
  only_all_tested = FALSE,
  guideline = getOption("AMR_guideline", "EUCAST")
)

Arguments

...

Two or more vectors (or columns) with antimicrobial interpretations, or a data frame with such columns. They will be transformed internally with as.sir() if needed. All vectors must be of the same length.

only_all_tested

A logical to indicate that isolates must be tested for all antimicrobials. If TRUE, the result is NA for isolates with a missing result for any of the antimicrobials. If FALSE (default), a missing result only leads to NA if a result for the missing antimicrobial could have changed the result of the combination, see Combination Therapy below.

guideline

Either "EUCAST" (default) or "CLSI", to determine whether the 'I' category is considered susceptible. This only affects isolates with a missing result for any of the antimicrobials when only_all_tested = FALSE, see Combination Therapy below. The default can be changed with the AMR_guideline option, see AMR-options.

Value

A sir vector with the same length as the input.

Combination Therapy

A combination of antimicrobials is considered as good as its most active antimicrobial: "S" is preferred over "WT", and "R" over "NWT" and "NS". The value "NI" (non-interpretable) is considered a missing result.

A missing result can only be ignored if the result of the combination is susceptible regardless of the missing result, which depends on the only_all_tested argument and on the guideline: under EUCAST, the 'I' category is considered susceptible (susceptible, increased exposure), and under CLSI, it is not.

This is an example for two antimicrobials, Drug A and Drug B (the order of the antimicrobials does not matter):

-------------------------------------------------------------------------
                            Result of the combination
                    -----------------------------------------------------
 Drug A    Drug B   only_all_tested = FALSE       only_all_tested = TRUE
--------  --------  ----------------------------  ----------------------
    S     S, I, R   S                             S
    I       I, R    I                             I
    R         R     R                             R
    S       <NA>    S                             <NA>
    I       <NA>    I (EUCAST), <NA> (CLSI)       <NA>
    R       <NA>    <NA>                          <NA>
  <NA>      <NA>    <NA>                          <NA>
-------------------------------------------------------------------------

The count_*() and proportion_*() functions, such as susceptibility() and resistance(), apply exactly these rules when more than one variable is used: an isolate is considered tested if the result of the combination is not NA, and is then counted by the result of the combination. Consequently, count_susceptible() + count_resistant() = count_all(), and susceptibility() + resistance() = 1, for both values of only_all_tested. The guideline is taken from their guideline argument if they have one, and otherwise from the AMR_guideline option.

In antibiogram() and wisca(), the 'I' and 'SDD' categories are considered susceptible if combine_SI = TRUE (default), and the result of the combination is then reduced to S or R.

See also

count() and proportion() for counting and calculating susceptibility of (combinations of) antimicrobials, and antibiogram() for combination antibiograms.

Examples

drug_a <- as.sir(c("S", "R", "R", "I", "I", NA, "R", "SDD"))
drug_b <- as.sir(c("R", "S", "R", "R", NA, NA, NA, "I"))

sir_combine(drug_a, drug_b)
#> Class <sir>
#> [1] S    S    R    I    I    <NA> <NA> SDD 
sir_combine(drug_a, drug_b, guideline = "CLSI")
#> Class <sir>
#> [1] S    S    R    I    <NA> <NA> <NA> SDD 
sir_combine(drug_a, drug_b, only_all_tested = TRUE)
#> Class <sir>
#> [1] S    S    R    I    <NA> <NA> <NA> SDD 

# the count and proportion functions use the same rules
susceptibility(drug_a, drug_b, minimum = 0)
#> Note that `proportion_SI()` will also include dose-dependent susceptibility,
#> "SDD". This note will be shown once for this session.
#> [1] 0.8333333
susceptibility(sir_combine(drug_a, drug_b), minimum = 0)
#> [1] 0.8333333

# \donttest{
if (require("dplyr")) {
  # create a new variable for piperacillin/tazobactam + gentamicin
  example_isolates %>%
    filter(!is.na(TZP)) %>%
    mutate(TZP_GEN = sir_combine(TZP, GEN)) %>%
    select(mo, TZP, GEN, TZP_GEN)
}
#> # A tibble: 1,001 × 4
#>    mo           TZP   GEN   TZP_GEN
#>    <mo>         <sir> <sir> <sir>  
#>  1 B_STRPT_SNGN   S     R     S    
#>  2 B_STRPT_GRPB   S     R     S    
#>  3 B_ESCHR_COLI   R     S     S    
#>  4 B_ESCHR_COLI   R     S     S    
#>  5 B_STRPT_PNMN   S     R     S    
#>  6 B_STRPT_PNMN   S     R     S    
#>  7 B_STRPT_ANGN   S     R     S    
#>  8 B_STRPT_ANGN   S     R     S    
#>  9 B_STRPT_PNMN   S     R     S    
#> 10 B_STRPT_SLVR   S     R     S    
#> # ℹ 991 more rows
if (require("dplyr")) {
  # combine any number of antimicrobials
  example_isolates %>%
    mutate(any_aminoglycoside = sir_combine(GEN, TOB, AMK, KAN)) %>%
    count(any_aminoglycoside)
}
#> # A tibble: 4 × 2
#>   any_aminoglycoside     n
#>   <sir>              <int>
#> 1   S                 1383
#> 2   I                   24
#> 3   R                  427
#> 4   NA                 166
if (require("dplyr")) {
  # use the new variable in further analyses
  # THOUGH CONSIDER wisca() FOR RELIABLE ESTIMATES
  example_isolates %>%
    mutate(TZP_GEN = sir_combine(TZP, GEN)) %>%
    group_by(ward) %>%
    summarise(
      TZP_mono = susceptibility(TZP),
      GEN_mono = susceptibility(GEN),
      TZP_GEN = susceptibility(TZP_GEN),
      # or directly, without combining first:
      TZP_GEN2 = susceptibility(TZP, GEN)
    )
}
#> # A tibble: 3 × 5
#>   ward       TZP_mono GEN_mono TZP_GEN TZP_GEN2
#>   <chr>         <dbl>    <dbl>   <dbl>    <dbl>
#> 1 Clinical      0.898    0.771   0.986    0.986
#> 2 ICU           0.819    0.710   0.962    0.962
#> 3 Outpatient    0.894    0.8     0.991    0.991
# }
